note: Five materially new source-linked records published after the 29 August wire. This is discovery material, not a numbered East Corner editorial conclusion; Signal 005 remains held because the set does not meet the two-primary-source foundation required for reviewed synthesis.

items.sourceHeadline: Kenya aviation workers end strike that disrupted flights, officials say
items.sourceDescription: Kenya's aviation workers ended a two-day strike after the union, aviation authorities and Jambojet signed a return-to-work agreement. The disruption delayed and cancelled flights linking Nairobi with airports across East Africa and beyond; negotiations continue over collective agreements and other grievances.
items.whyItMatters: The stoppage exposed how labour relations at Nairobi's main aviation hub can propagate quickly through regional passenger and cargo networks. Service has resumed, but the underlying labour disputes are not settled.
items.inferenceOrUnresolved: The agreement restores operations while leaving the outstanding collective-bargaining and workplace issues under negotiation.

items.sourceHeadline: Ethiopian Airlines nears Boeing cargo plane order, sources say
items.sourceDescription: Two industry sources told Reuters that Ethiopian Airlines was nearing an order for eight to 10 Boeing 777 freighters, potentially including two current-generation 777Fs and later 777-8Fs. Neither Boeing nor Ethiopian Airlines confirmed the negotiations; the carrier is also helping finance a $12.5-billion airport project at Bishoftu.
items.whyItMatters: A larger freighter fleet would deepen Addis Ababa's position as an African cargo hub alongside the planned airport expansion. The commercial terms, delivery timetable and final aircraft mix remain unconfirmed.
items.inferenceOrUnresolved: This is a reported negotiation, not an announced order; Boeing and Ethiopian Airlines did not confirm it.

items.sourceHeadline: Kenyan editor found safe after abduction, employer says
items.sourceDescription: Standard Group said associate editor Alex Kiprotich was abducted near Nakuru by armed men and released hours later near Masinga Dam, more than 200 km away. The company's chief executive said the abductors demanded the newspaper's sources; police opened an investigation while criticizing aspects of the newspaper's reporting.
items.whyItMatters: The case puts source protection and journalist safety back into Kenya's institutional record. Kiprotich's safe recovery does not resolve who carried out the abduction or whether anyone will be held accountable.
items.inferenceOrUnresolved: The abductors' identities, the circumstances of release and accountability outcome remain unresolved.

items.sourceHeadline: Kenya private sector activity slows in August, PMI shows
items.sourceDescription: The Stanbic Bank Kenya Purchasing Managers' Index fell to 49.7 in August from 51.3 in July, moving below the 50 threshold that separates expansion from contraction. Survey respondents cited supply constraints, higher raw-material costs and tight cash flow even as demand strengthened.
items.whyItMatters: The reading suggests demand alone is not translating into output when firms face input and liquidity constraints. One monthly survey does not establish a durable downturn.
items.inferenceOrUnresolved: The PMI is a survey indicator rather than a complete measure of national output, and the duration of the contraction signal is unknown.

items.sourceHeadline: Foreign support, drones fuel Sudan war and possible war crimes, UN probe says
items.sourceDescription: A U.N. fact-finding mission said foreign weapons, technology, fighters and logistics are sustaining Sudan's war and expanding both sides' drone reach. It recorded more than 1,000 deaths from drone strikes in the first five months of 2026 and said some operations may amount to war crimes; parties named in the report disputed or did not answer allegations.
items.whyItMatters: The report connects external supply networks to civilian harm and the destruction of essential infrastructure far from front lines. Its allegations require careful attribution because several governments and both Sudanese belligerents contest responsibility.
items.inferenceOrUnresolved: The UAE denied supplying military materiel, Somalia cited information-sharing gaps while denying authorized support, and investigations into external support for Sudan's army remain at an early stage.
